context: await this.db.tx('studio', (q) => this.refuseIfHeld(q, who, spans), { readOnly: true });
why: Leases.check and list only read: with no other writer at the same time they give the same answers. What differs is the locking, not the result: on SQLite a read-only transaction is a plain BEGIN (a WAL snapshot) and the mutant's BEGIN IMMEDIATE takes the write lock, so under contention it waits (or throws StoreBusy after its wait) where the original reads; on Postgres the isolation is REPEATABLE READ rather than READ COMMITTED. Neither changes what a lease check or a listing answers

context: if (!p || Number(p.expires_at) <= now || Number(p.last_seen) + SESSION_MS <= now)
why: Play.handle: a game session's expiry is set to at most 15 min after its last use, each time it is used (min(now + 15 min, the Studio session's end)), so `last_seen + 15 min <= now` never holds while `expires_at <= now` does not: the second boundary never decides (the first is pinned to the millisecond by tests/studio-play-mutants.test.ts)

backupOf's row order: `<` and `<=` differ only for two rows whose canonical JSON is the same, and two such rows are the same row written twice, so whichever comes first the table's JSON (and its digest) is the same (the order itself is pinned by tests/studio-workshop-backup-mutants.test.ts)
Shipper's `wanted` is read only by the loop `ship()` starts, and `ship()` sets it to true before starting it: its initial value is never read

Shipper.close: `clearTimeout(null)` does nothing, so clearing a timer that is not there is the guard skipped (that a pending retry is cleared is pinned by tests/studio-workshop-backup-mutants.test.ts)
Health's `wanted` is read by the loop and by the end of a run, both started by `schedule()`, which sets it to true first: its initial value is never read

Health.schedule after close: without the early return the loop starts, but its `while (this.wanted && !this.closed)` runs no turn, and the run's end does not ask again (`!this.closed`); nothing is judged either way (pinned by tests/studio-workshop-health-mutants.test.ts), only the promise returned is another, already settled one

context: if (rev > head) throw new Error(`revision ${rev} is past the head (${head})`);
why: Health.judge's guard: its two callers never pass a revision past the head: the loop bisects below its snapshot's revision, which is the head, and bisectOn refuses `bad > head` and `good >= bad` before judging (its refusal is pinned by tests/studio-health.test.ts); the guard is a defence for a future caller

serveAsset: `end` is at most `size - 1` (no range, `Math.min(…, size - 1)` or `size - 1`), so `start >= size` already makes `start > end` true; the second test never decides, and `start === size` is refused by the first (the ranges are pinned by tests/studio-workshop-previews-mutants.test.ts)
